still_open.lead: Change the OUTPUT format away from AVIF. The official HTB forum thread (primary source, spoiler-free) has a player asking 'How to bypass the .avif extension?!!', another told to read the challenge's Dockerfile to find 'the key tool(s) involved', and one reporting trouble with filenames containing periods. A third says 'the library in the code is just a wrapper to the CLI', which a pure sharp/libvips binding is not.
still_open.supporting_measurement: the accepted-format matrix is PNG, GIF, BMP, JPEG and PPM; TIFF, WebP, MVG, SVG and plain text are refused. libvips supports TIFF and WebP, so an unmodified sharp does not fit that set.
still_open.falsifier: identify the tool from its own documentation and find every documented way its output format is decided; if none is reachable from file content alone, the lead is dead.

still_open.lead: The redacted pixels are NOT recoverable from the served file -- that is measured. So either the flag is not under the red boxes, or the challenge yields a DIFFERENT file (an original on disk, or an arbitrary read).
still_open.supporting_measurement: two AVIF items only; alpha is 74 bytes and uniform; no original at any derivable path.
still_open.falsifier: if an arbitrary file read exists, the flag is a file, not a pixel region.

honest_conclusion: Unsolved. Seventeen layers closed by measurement in one session, including every input I control (rotate, flip, message, parentId, filename, content-type, extra keys, the file bytes across nine formats) and every artifact route. The authored feature is a server-side rotate/flip pipeline that re-encodes to AVIF, and the one primary source available says its library shells out to a CLI named in the challenge's Dockerfile -- which I do not have. The open lead is the output format, not the pixels: the redaction is baked into the colour plane and nothing in the container hides anything.
